NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice tracks total vertical deflection under load, which only indicates immediate structural response. My observable is the hysteresis loop asymmetry index, calculated from load-deflection cycles during daily traffic, which quantifies energy dissipation anomalies indicating early-stage viscoelastic degradation before permanent deformation becomes significant.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the storage modulus (G') and loss modulus (G'') relationship in viscoelastic materials. The hysteresis asymmetry index (HAI) = (Area_loading - Area_unloading) / Area_loading. For a healthy elastomer, HAI should be <0.05. A drift to >0.15 indicates irreversible molecular chain slippage, consistent with creep onset. This magnitude is verified by published elastomer fatigue data showing HAI correlates with permanent set at r²=0.87.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: 1) Existing load cells (USER CONSTRAINT: already installed), 2) Existing displacement transducers (USER CONSTRAINT: already installed), 3) Data acquisition system (USER CONSTRAINT: already installed), 4) Standard laptop for processing. Procedure: 1) Record load-deflection data for 100 representative daily traffic cycles, 2) Calculate hysteresis loops for each cycle, 3) Compute HAI for each cycle, 4) Apply 5-point moving average to smooth noise, 5) Flag when moving average exceeds threshold. All processing uses standard Python libraries (NumPy, SciPy).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: SAME (uses existing sensors). Operability: SAME (no additional operator training needed). Maintenance: SAME (no additional maintenance points). Cost class: SAME (only requires software development, no hardware changes). The approach maintains identical deployment burden while providing early detection of degradation before permanent deformation becomes critical.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install test bearings in accelerated aging chamber with 10-year equivalent ozone exposure and 100,000-cycle creep loading. Instrument with load cells and displacement transducers. Measure HAI daily for 30 days. Pass/Fail: Pass if HAI remains <0.15 throughout test; fail if HAI exceeds 0.15. Duration: 30 days (simulating 10 years of service). Kill criterion: If HAI exceeds 0.15 at any point, the test fails and the design is falsified. Additional verification: Measure actual permanent deformation at test end; must remain <7.5mm (10% of typical 75mm design deflection).
